system: the Taliban is implementing its own interpretation of Islamic law, which is partially based on the Hanifi school of Islamic jurisprudence and have enforced strict punishments; before the Taliban takeover, Afghanistan had a mixed legal system of civil, customary, and Islamic law (2021)

constitution.history: several previous; latest ratified in 2004, but not currently enforced by the Taliban

courts.highest: the Taliban are purported to have appointed clerics, including a "Chief Justice," to Afghanistan's Supreme Court
courts.lower: provincial courts, religious courts, and specialty courts

citizenship.descent: at least one parent must have been born in - and continuously lived in - Afghanistan

world: has not submitted an ICJ jurisdiction declaration; formerly accepted ICCt jurisdiction
